actions.title: Create the Render web service (Docker) in Ohio (slug: ohio)
actions.detail: Select Docker as the service language and set the Dockerfile path if the file is outside the repository root. The server must listen on 0.0.0.0 at PORT (default 10000); deployment fails when no listening port is detected.

actions.title: Create the Neon project in AWS US East, Ohio (slug: aws-us-east-2)
actions.detail: Pick the region near the application (aws-us-east-2 for US or aws-eu-central-1 for EU), then select the branch, database and role to obtain the pooled and the direct connection strings.

actions.title: Create the Backblaze B2 account in the target region and create a private bucket
actions.detail: The B2 account region is chosen at account creation (e.g. us-east-005 or eu-central-003). New buckets default to Private (allPrivate) and are versioned by default; B2 supports only bucket-level canned ACLs (private and public-read) and rejects object-level ACL overrides with 403 Forbidden.

actions.title: Scope the B2 key and Neon application role
actions.detail: Do not use the account Master Application Key (incompatible with the S3 API). Generate a dedicated Application Key restricted to this single bucket (and optional fileNamePrefix) with Read/Write permissions; map keyID to S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and applicationKey to S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Create a dedicated application role using SQL, with only the database, schema, table and sequence privileges the application requires. Do not use the default owner or a default console/API role as the application identity. Review public privileges, role memberships, row-level security and privileges on future objects for the actual schema. Keep the migration identity separate. Verify required operations succeed and prohibited operations fail before switching application credentials.
gaps: Verify application-specific grants, inherited/public privileges, row-level security and future-object privileges; record successful allowed-operation and denied-operation checks before switching credentials.

actions.title: Attach a custom domain to the API
actions.detail: Point the API hostname at the Render service only after Render accepts the domain. For the Render API, add the domain in service Settings, follow the DNS-provider instructions linked in the Render custom-domain docs, remove conflicting AAAA records, then click Verify. Check workspace custom-domain quotas and charges.

actions.title: Set the real values on the Render service
actions.detail: Copy each key from .env.example into the service environment variables or a secret file. Never commit real values.

actions.title: Run schema migrations over the direct connection
actions.detail: Use the direct (non-pooled) Neon connection string for migrations before the new release takes traffic; the application keeps the pooled string.

actions.title: Verify TLS on the database and the API
actions.detail: Connect to Neon with sslmode=verify-full and confirm that a plain HTTP request to the API is redirected to HTTPS.

actions.title: Configure and pass the Render health check
actions.detail: The health-check path must answer with a 2xx or 3xx status within five seconds.

actions.title: Upload, read back and delete one test object
actions.detail: Through the API, upload a small object to the bucket (PutObject / Multipart Upload / SigV4 presigned URL), read it back (GetObject / HeadObject), then delete it (DeleteObject). Because B2 buckets are versioned by default, standard single-object delete calls create a delete marker or remove only the latest version unless older versions are explicitly purged.

actions.title: Patch the container base image
actions.detail: Render maintains the host platform. The application owner reviews and updates the Docker base image and installed packages, rebuilds, tests and redeploys the image. Check build-cache behavior and pin a reproducible image digest; record the responsible owner and update cadence.
gaps: Verify the deployed image digest and base-image/package patch status; record rebuild, test and deployment evidence, the responsible owner and update cadence.

actions.title: Run a database restore drill
actions.detail: Restore the database into a non-production target and run the health check against it before you depend on backups. Inspect the configured Neon history window first: Free supports six hours capped at 1 GB of history; Launch defaults to one day and allows up to seven days. A zero window disables instant restore. Paid history storage is a separate unmodeled cost.
gaps: Verify the actual project history window, retained recovery point, history-storage cost and restore-drill result.

actions.title: Track certificate and domain expiry
actions.detail: Record the domain renewal date with your registrar and confirm that the certificate for the custom domain renews. Render documents automatic custom-domain certificate issuance and renewal; verify the live certificate and monitoring for your domain.
gaps: Domain renewal terms depend on the user's registrar.
Certificate expiry monitoring and alert delivery require project-specific verification.

actions.title: Roll back a bad release
actions.detail: In Render Deploys, select a successful deployment with a retained build artifact and confirm Rollback to this deploy. Dashboard rollback disables automatic deploys; reenable them only after resolving the issue. API rollback does not disable them. Disks are not rolled back. For registry images use an available immutable digest. Review database migration compatibility separately; a provider application rollback does not prove that a reverse migration is safe.
gaps: Project-specific migration rollback safety and recovery procedure require verification.

actions.title: Tear down every resource
actions.detail: Delete all objects and versions in the Backblaze B2 bucket and delete the empty bucket in B2 Cloud Storage, Buckets, Bucket Settings, Delete Bucket, then delete the scoped B2 Application Key in Application Keys (or via b2_delete_key). Delete the Render web service in service Settings or with render services delete <service> --confirm, and delete the Neon project in Settings, General, Delete project (seven-day recovery period; deleting projects does not itself stop paid-plan billing).
gaps: Physical backup purge timing and final billing/retention outcomes after resource deletion require account verification.
